title.es: Leer el guion de una escena

es: Leer un guion breve y distinguir diálogo, acotaciones y subtexto, explicando lo que un personaje quiere decir en realidad.

teaching.en: The script shows what each character says and what each character does.
teaching.es: El guion muestra lo que dice y lo que hace cada personaje.
teaching.explanationEs: Un guion mezcla diálogo (lo que se dice) y acotaciones (lo que se hace).
segments: The script shows what each character
says and what each character does.
teaching.audioText: The script shows what each character says and what each character does.

teaching.en: A stage direction tells the actor how the character moves, looks or speaks: (She whispers.)
teaching.es: Una acotación le dice al actor cómo se mueve, mira o habla el personaje: (Ella susurra.)
teaching.explanationEs: Las acotaciones van entre paréntesis y se escriben en presente; nadie las pronuncia.
segments: A stage direction tells the actor how the
character moves, looks or speaks: (She whispers.)
teaching.audioText: A stage direction tells the actor how the character moves, looks or speaks: (She whispers.)

teaching.en: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud.
teaching.es: La frase «Estoy bien» es diálogo, porque el personaje la dice en voz alta.
teaching.explanationEs: Diálogo = lo que un personaje pronuncia en voz alta.
segments: The line «I am fine» is dialogue,
because the character says it aloud.
teaching.audioText: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud.

teaching.en: The subtext is what the character hides: she says «I am fine», but she means «I am worried».
teaching.es: El subtexto es lo que el personaje oculta: dice «Estoy bien», pero quiere decir «Estoy preocupada».
teaching.explanationEs: Says … but means …: la fórmula para explicar el subtexto.
segments: The subtext is what the character hides: she says
«I am fine», but she means «I am worried».
teaching.audioText: The subtext is what the character hides: she says «I am fine», but she means «I am worried».

teaching.en: A long pause can show the subtext of a scene.
teaching.es: Una pausa larga puede mostrar el subtexto de una escena.
teaching.explanationEs: Las pausas, los cambios de tema y las respuestas cortas son pistas del subtexto.
segments: A long pause can show
the subtext of a scene.
teaching.audioText: A long pause can show the subtext of a scene.

teaching.en: In this scene, the character asks about the weather because he wants to avoid the real topic.
teaching.es: En esta escena, el personaje pregunta por el tiempo porque quiere evitar el tema real.
teaching.explanationEs: Evitar el tema real también es subtexto: lo importante no se dice.
segments: In this scene, the character asks about the weather
because he wants to avoid the real topic.
teaching.audioText: In this scene, the character asks about the weather because he wants to avoid the real topic.

prompt.es: Clasifica esta línea de un guion: ¿diálogo, acotación o subtexto?

choices.text: a stage direction
a line of dialogue
subtext

feedback.es: Va entre paréntesis y describe lo que Ana hace (mira y susurra): es una acotación, no algo que se diga en voz alta.

hint.es: Fíjate en si lo dice un personaje o si describe lo que hace.

origin.text: (Ana looks at the door and whispers.)

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que un personaje quiere decir pero no dice se llama subtexto.»

answer.text: subtext

feedback.es: El subtexto es el significado que queda debajo de las palabras y que el personaje no pronuncia.

hint.es: Es el significado escondido debajo de las palabras.

origin.text: What a character means but does not say is called ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El guion muestra lo que dice cada personaje.»

answer.text: The script shows what each character says

feedback.es: Después de what va sujeto + verbo en orden afirmativo: what each character says.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto: el guion.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada línea de la escena con su tipo.

pairs: (Tom sits down and whispers.)
«Fine. Do what you like.»
He is angry but hides it.

feedback.es: Lo que se hace va entre paréntesis (acotación), lo que se dice es diálogo y lo que se oculta es subtexto.

pairs: (Tom sits down and whispers.)
«Fine. Do what you like.»
He is angry but hides it.

prompt.es: Lee la escena: ¿qué oculta Leo en realidad?

choices.text: He is excited about the next song.
He is tired and wants to leave.
He wants Mia to dance with him.

prompt.es: Explica el subtexto en una frase con «says … but means …».

answer.text: Tom says the food is great, but he means he does not like it.
accepted: Tom says the food is great, but he means he does not like it.
Tom says that the food is great, but he means that he does not like it.
Tom says the food is great, but he means it is not good.

feedback.es: La acotación muestra que no come: el gesto contradice el diálogo, así que Tom quiere decir que no le gusta.

origin.text: TOM: The food is great. (He leaves the food on his plate.)

prompt.es: Escucha la línea y elige lo que el personaje quiere decir.

choices.text: He is happy about the rain.
He wants to stay outside longer.
He is annoyed that he has to wait.

feedback.es: Dice «great» y «just what I wanted» sobre algo desagradable: el subtexto es que está molesto por esperar.

prompt.es: Elige la función de esta línea en un guion.

choices.text: It describes the action and mood of the scene.
It is what a character says aloud.
It explains what a character hides.

feedback.es: Describe lo que se ve y el ambiente, no lo que alguien pronuncia: es una acotación.

origin.text: (The two friends sit in silence. Rain hits the window.)

prompt.es: Completa las tres definiciones de un guion.

answer.text: do | says | means

feedback.es: La acotación describe lo que hacen los personajes, el diálogo se dice y el subtexto es lo que quieren decir.

accepted: Ana says she is fine, but she means she is worried.

prompt.es: Elige el subtexto de esta respuesta.

choices.text: He is relaxed and wants to talk.

feedback.es: Dice que no está enfadado, pero su negativa a hablar muestra que lo está y lo oculta.

feedback.es: La pausa es una pista: muestra lo que el personaje no dice.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada gesto con lo que revela.

pairs: He says yes but shakes his head.

feedback.es: Los gestos contradicen o completan las palabras: apuntan a lo que el personaje no dice.

es: Usar adjetivos evaluativos precisos para describir trama, actuación y ritmo de una película y destacar lo que más gustó.

teaching.en: The plot is gripping: we never know what will happen next.
teaching.es: La trama es absorbente: nunca sabemos qué pasará después.
teaching.explanationEs: Gripping describe una trama o un ritmo que te mantiene pendiente de la pantalla.
segments: The plot is gripping: we never
know what will happen next.
teaching.audioText: The plot is gripping: we never know what will happen next.

teaching.en: The plot is far-fetched because nobody would do that in real life.
teaching.es: La trama es inverosímil porque nadie haría eso en la vida real.
teaching.explanationEs: Far-fetched = difícil de creer; se dice de una trama o situación, no de una persona.
segments: The plot is far-fetched because nobody
would do that in real life.
teaching.audioText: The plot is far-fetched because nobody would do that in real life.

teaching.en: Her performance was understated: she says little but shows a lot.
teaching.es: Su interpretación fue contenida: dice poco pero muestra mucho.
teaching.explanationEs: Understated = sin exageración; es lo contrario de over the top.
segments: Her performance was understated: she says
little but shows a lot.
teaching.audioText: Her performance was understated: she says little but shows a lot.

teaching.en: The acting felt wooden because the actors spoke without any feeling.
teaching.es: La actuación resultó acartonada porque los actores hablaban sin ningún sentimiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Wooden se aplica a una actuación rígida y sin emoción; el sustantivo es acting.
segments: The acting felt wooden because the
actors spoke without any feeling.
teaching.audioText: The acting felt wooden because the actors spoke without any feeling.

teaching.en: The pace is slow at first, but the ending is moving.
teaching.es: El ritmo es lento al principio, pero el final es conmovedor.
teaching.explanationEs: Pace = ritmo; moving = conmovedor (no «en movimiento»). Se dice the ending is moving.
segments: The pace is slow at first,
but the ending is moving.
teaching.audioText: The pace is slow at first, but the ending is moving.

teaching.en: What I liked most was the convincing performance of the old actor.
teaching.es: Lo que más me gustó fue la interpretación convincente del actor mayor.
teaching.explanationEs: Oración enfática con What … was: destaca lo que más te impresionó.
segments: What I liked most was the
convincing performance of the old actor.
teaching.audioText: What I liked most was the convincing performance of the old actor.

prompt.es: Elige el adjetivo que describe esta trama de película.

choices.text: The plot is understated.
The plot is far-fetched.
The acting is convincing.

feedback.es: Un pájaro que deja caer la llave a los pies de la profesora es demasiada casualidad: nadie lo creería, así que la trama es inverosímil.

hint.es: Piensa si una situación así podría pasar en la vida real.

origin.text: The actor's performance was ___: he says little and shows a lot.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo que más me gustó fue el ritmo.»

answer.text: What I liked most was the pace

feedback.es: En la oración enfática, What + oración va primero y was introduce lo destacado.

hint.es: Empieza por What y termina con el aspecto elegido.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada reseña breve con el adjetivo que resume el juicio.

pairs: I could not stop watching: every scene made me want more.
A dog becomes the mayor and nobody asks why.
I knew the ending after ten minutes.
The actors spoke without any feeling.
When the old man said goodbye, the whole room felt sad.

feedback.es: Cada juicio apunta a un aspecto: no poder dejar de mirar es absorbente; adivinar el final, predecible.

pairs: I could not stop watching: every scene made me want more.

choices.text: It criticises the acting: it is over the top.
It criticises the script: the dialogue is unnatural.

accepted: The actor's performance was convincing because it felt real.
The performance was convincing because it felt real.
His performance was convincing because he looked real.

feedback.es: Adjetivo evaluativo + because: convincing resume la interpretación y la razón es que parece real.

es: Comprender la actitud de los personajes en una escena de audio a partir de las palabras, las pausas y el tono, y describirla con sounds + adjetivo.

teaching.en: Leo sounds defensive because he answers every question with another question.
teaching.es: Leo suena a la defensiva porque responde a cada pregunta con otra pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: Sounds + adjetivo (sin -ly): así describes la actitud que oyes.
segments: Leo sounds defensive because he answers
every question with another question.
teaching.audioText: Leo sounds defensive because he answers every question with another question.

teaching.en: Her tone is sarcastic: she says «great», but she does not mean it.
teaching.es: Su tono es sarcástico: dice «genial», pero no lo piensa.
teaching.explanationEs: El sarcasmo dice lo contrario de lo que se piensa; el tono y el contexto son las pistas.
segments: Her tone is sarcastic: she says «great»,
but she does not mean it.
teaching.audioText: Her tone is sarcastic: she says «great», but she does not mean it.

teaching.en: The long pause is a clue that he is hesitant.
teaching.es: La pausa larga es una pista de que él duda.
teaching.explanationEs: Las pausas y los «well…» indican duda; la pista apoya tu juicio sobre la actitud.
segments: The long pause is a
clue that he is hesitant.
teaching.audioText: The long pause is a clue that he is hesitant.

teaching.en: Mia sounds anxious, so Tom tries to reassure her.
teaching.es: Mia suena ansiosa, así que Tom intenta tranquilizarla.
teaching.explanationEs: Reassure = tranquilizar dando seguridad; anxious = con ansiedad.
segments: Mia sounds anxious, so Tom
tries to reassure her.
teaching.audioText: Mia sounds anxious, so Tom tries to reassure her.

teaching.en: A dismissive attitude shows in short answers like «Whatever».
teaching.es: Una actitud desdeñosa se nota en respuestas cortas como «Lo que sea».
teaching.explanationEs: Dismissive = quita importancia a lo que dice el otro.
segments: A dismissive attitude shows in
short answers like «Whatever».
teaching.audioText: A dismissive attitude shows in short answers like «Whatever».

teaching.en: He is evasive: he never answers the question, so the teacher becomes suspicious.
teaching.es: Es evasivo: nunca responde a la pregunta, así que la profesora desconfía.
teaching.explanationEs: Evasive = esquiva las preguntas; suspicious = desconfía de lo que oye.
segments: He is evasive: he never answers the
question, so the teacher becomes suspicious.
teaching.audioText: He is evasive: he never answers the question, so the teacher becomes suspicious.

choices.text: He is anxious about the plan.
He is hesitant about the plan.
He is dismissive about the plan.

feedback.es: Responde con «whatever» y dice que no le importa: quita importancia a lo que propone el otro.

hint.es: Escucha qué palabras usa y si muestra interés por el plan.

hint.es: Después de sounds va un adjetivo: describe cómo se siente.

hint.es: Primero la actitud del personaje; la razón va después de because.

choices.text: He is unsure and delays the answer.

es: Reseñar una escena con presente narrativo, dos oraciones enfáticas y una valoración razonada.

teaching.en: In the climax, the teacher opens the door and freezes.
teaching.es: En el clímax, la profesora abre la puerta y se queda inmóvil.
teaching.explanationEs: Presente narrativo: cuentas la escena en presente aunque ya la viste (opens, freezes).
segments: In the climax, the teacher
opens the door and freezes.
teaching.audioText: In the climax, the teacher opens the door and freezes.

teaching.en: The moment she reveals the secret, the whole room falls silent.
teaching.es: En el momento en que revela el secreto, toda la sala se queda en silencio.
teaching.explanationEs: Reveals y falls: todos los verbos de la escena van en presente.
segments: The moment she reveals the secret,
the whole room falls silent.
teaching.audioText: The moment she reveals the secret, the whole room falls silent.

teaching.en: What makes the scene gripping is the silence, not the dialogue.
teaching.es: Lo que hace absorbente la escena es el silencio, no el diálogo.
teaching.explanationEs: Oración enfática con What … is: destaca lo más importante.
segments: What makes the scene gripping is
the silence, not the dialogue.
teaching.audioText: What makes the scene gripping is the silence, not the dialogue.

teaching.en: It is the small detail of the empty chair that conveys her sadness.
teaching.es: Es el pequeño detalle de la silla vacía lo que transmite su tristeza.
teaching.explanationEs: It is … that: otra oración enfática para destacar un elemento.
segments: It is the small detail of the
empty chair that conveys her sadness.
teaching.audioText: It is the small detail of the empty chair that conveys her sadness.

teaching.en: The long silence builds tension because nobody knows who will speak first.
teaching.es: El largo silencio crea tensión porque nadie sabe quién hablará primero.
teaching.explanationEs: Valoración razonada: di qué efecto produce y por qué con because.
segments: The long silence builds tension because
nobody knows who will speak first.
teaching.audioText: The long silence builds tension because nobody knows who will speak first.

teaching.en: Overall, this moment is a turning point, because the audience learns the truth.
teaching.es: En conjunto, este momento es un punto de inflexión, porque el público conoce la verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Cierra con una valoración y una razón: is a turning point because…
segments: Overall, this moment is a turning point,
because the audience learns the truth.
teaching.audioText: Overall, this moment is a turning point, because the audience learns the truth.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cuenta la escena en presente narrativo?

choices.text: The girl opens the letter and starts to smile.
The girl opened the letter and starts to smile.
The girl is opened the letter and smiled.

feedback.es: En el presente narrativo todos los verbos van en presente: opens … starts.

hint.es: Mira que todos los verbos estén en el mismo tiempo.

prompt.es: Reseña la escena: presente narrativo, dos oraciones enfáticas y una valoración razonada.

answer.text: In the scene at the station, an old woman waits alone on a bench. A young man sits next to her and gives her a letter that she lost many years ago. She looks at the envelope, touches it and says nothing for ten seconds. Then she smiles. What makes this moment so moving is the silence: nobody speaks, but we understand everything. It is the small detail of her hands that conveys her feelings, because they shake a little when she touches the letter. The performance is understated, and the pace is slow, which gives the scene its tension. Overall, I think this is the best moment of the film because it suggests a whole life without a single line of dialogue. It is a turning point, and the audience feels the truth before the woman says a word.
accepted: In the scene at the station, an old woman waits alone on a bench. A young man sits next to her and gives her a letter that she lost many years ago. She looks at the envelope, touches it and says nothing for ten seconds. Then she smiles. What makes this moment so moving is the silence: nobody speaks, but we understand everything. It is the small detail of her hands that conveys her feelings, because they shake a little when she touches the letter. The performance is understated, and the pace is slow, which gives the scene its tension. Overall, I think this is the best moment of the film because it suggests a whole life without a single line of dialogue. It is a turning point, and the audience feels the truth before the woman says a word.

In the final scene, a boy opens the door of an empty house and freezes. A letter lies on the floor. He reads it slowly, and his face changes. What I liked most was the silence, because nobody explains the moment. It is the music that builds the tension, and it stops at the perfect second. The acting is understated: he says nothing, but his eyes show everything. Overall, the scene is gripping and moving because it trusts the audience. It suggests more than it tells, and that is why it is the turning point of the story. I would watch it again just for this moment.

feedback.es: Una buena reseña narra en presente, destaca lo más importante con what/it is … that y justifica la valoración con because.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención en el cineclub: recomienda, describe una escena y responde.

answer.text: I would recommend The Last Lighthouse because the script is gripping and the performance of the old actor is understated and convincing. I see your point about the pace: it is slow at first, and some people say the film is overrated. Even so, I would argue that the slow start is worth it. In the key scene, the old keeper opens the door of the lighthouse and freezes: the room is empty and his daughter's chair is broken. What makes this moment so moving is the silence, because nobody says a word. It is the small detail of the chair that conveys his sadness. Fair enough, the plot is not perfect, but the ending is a turning point that stays with you. It is worth watching twice, and I would rewatch it with friends.
accepted: I would recommend The Last Lighthouse because the script is gripping and the performance of the old actor is understated and convincing. I see your point about the pace: it is slow at first, and some people say the film is overrated. Even so, I would argue that the slow start is worth it. In the key scene, the old keeper opens the door of the lighthouse and freezes: the room is empty and his daughter's chair is broken. What makes this moment so moving is the silence, because nobody says a word. It is the small detail of the chair that conveys his sadness. Fair enough, the plot is not perfect, but the ending is a turning point that stays with you. It is worth watching twice, and I would rewatch it with friends.

I would recommend The Last Lighthouse because it is a moving film with a convincing story. I see your objection, and the pace is slow. Even so, I would argue that the slow pace builds tension and that this is the reason why the ending is so strong. In the last scene, the keeper walks up the stairs and stops at the top. He looks at the sea and says nothing. What I liked most was the silence, because the film trusts the audience and does not explain every detail. It is the pause that shows his fear. Fair enough, the film is not for everyone, but it is worth watching twice, and I would rewatch it with my family.

feedback.es: La intervención completa recomienda con because, narra la escena en presente con what/it is … that y responde con I see your point y even so.
